rationale: The base station lost its internet uplink (E-503, no_internet) after the customer's router was replaced, causing all devices to appear offline in the app. A proper power-cycle sequence (router first, then base station) restored connectivity: the LED turned solid blue, the app showed all devices online on mobile data, and a real door-open notification was delivered, confirming the cloud uplink is working again. The console's stale "no_internet" reading did not refresh, but customer-verified cloud notifications confirm full recovery.

repair_steps: Power-cycle the router: unplug power, wait 30 seconds, plug back in, wait 2 minutes.
Power-cycle the base station: unplug power, wait 30 seconds, plug back in, wait 2-3 minutes.
Verify base station LED turns solid blue.
Confirm in app on mobile data that all devices show online and notifications are received.
output.customer_reply: I'm glad we got everything back online! The issue was that your base station lost its internet connection after the router replacement. Power-cycling the router first, then the base station, restored the connection. Your system is now fully working, including notifications. If you notice any further issues, please don't hesitate to reach out. Safe travels!

args.query: E-503 base station no internet uplink after router replacement

args.question: How is the base station connected to the internet — by Ethernet cable to the new router, or over Wi-Fi? And what color is the LED on the base station right now (solid green, blinking red, etc.)?

args.action: Check the back of the base station: is there an Ethernet cable plugged into its LAN/WAN port, and does the other end go into one of the new router's LAN ports (not the WAN/Internet port)? If it was on Wi-Fi before, the new router has different Wi-Fi name/password, so the base station can't reconnect. Please confirm whether an Ethernet cable is connected, and if so, that it's firmly seated in both the base station and a LAN port on the new router.

Let's power-cycle in the correct order. 1) Unplug power from the new router, wait 30 seconds, plug it back in and wait 2 full minutes until its internet light is stable. 2) Then unplug power from the base station, wait 30 seconds, and plug it back in. Wait 2-3 minutes, then tell me what color the base station LED is and whether the app still shows everything grey.

args.question: Now that the app shows everything back online, can you confirm: when you open the app on mobile data (not your home Wi-Fi), does it still say the base station is unreachable? And do you receive a test notification when you trigger a sensor (e.g., open the front door)?

results.text: The base station could not deliver events to the cloud. Frontline action: verify internet access, restart router and base station, set router DNS to automatic. If E-503 persists after these steps while the base station is online, escalate to FAE (cloud channel or certificate issue).

Base station online, live view works on local network, but no event notifications; E-503 every few minutes. Router restart and DNS reset did not help. Escalated; expired device certificate on backend. Escalated correctly.

The base station connects to the home router by Ethernet (recommended) or 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. If all cameras and sensors show offline in the app at the same time, first check whether the base station itself is online. Power-cycle the router, wait 2 minutes, then power-cycle the base station. The base station requires outbound TCP 443 and 8883 to the cloud.

complaint: Hi, everything in my security app went grey around 7 this morning: all my cameras and sensors show offline and I get no notifications at all. Yesterday afternoon our internet provider's technician replaced the router, and since then the Wi-Fi on my laptop works fine. I tried opening the app on mobile data and it says the base station is unreachable. I'm travelling next week, so I need this working. I think the base station has died.
usability_reason: The response is clear, polite, and actionable, listing the exact steps performed and verification checks. It accurately reflects the session record: the customer did power-cycle the router then base station, the LED turned solid blue, the app showed devices online on mobile data, and a notification was received. It avoids claiming any unperformed checks or fixes and correctly attributes the issue to lost internet connection after router replacement without overclaiming a specific root cause beyond what was observed.
